# TERMs with `tags` `self-governance`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Self-governance** — governing oneself by standards that are one's own — identification and wholeheartedness, planning agency and policies, self-constitution, autonomy and authenticity, and the empirical psychology of self-endorsed motives. One of four unities kept apart (group: philosophy; ADR-024).

| [TERM-060](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-060.md) v2 | frustration, of an organization's demands: the failure of the demands it maintains to be jointly realizable under its admissible transformations and its governance | A33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U33, made ordinal by the owner's U37 correction. The demands an organization maintains are frustrated when no admissible transformation meets them all (structural) or when one exists and the organization's governance does not select it (governance-induced). In its basic form it is an empty intersection of acceptance sets and needs no common scale. It is distinct from strain, where the demands are jointly realizable at a cost, and from distress, a possible integrated response to either. It is not [CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md)'s physics sense, though it shares that sense's three-demand minimal obstruction. | Active |
| [TERM-061](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-061.md) | practical synchronization: an agent's action-generating regimes, relative to a context and a horizon, sustaining mutually compatible courses of activity through their own interactions, without recurrent overriding arbitration by a higher level, whether or not they rank the same course first | The broader sense the owner asked for at U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17 ("we should probably propose a more general definition for this term"), defined from A45.
